entities.summary:
Basil Hall (1788–1844) was a Scottish Royal Navy officer, traveller, and author whose voyage narratives brought Pacific, East Asian, and Latin American shores to British readers in the generation after Cook. Son of the geologist Sir James Hall of Dunglass, he combined naval hydrography with a scientific curiosity shaped by Edinburgh Enlightenment circles.

Hall’s published voyages—including accounts of Korea, Chile, Peru, and Mexico—mixed seamanship, ethnography, and political observation during the age of Latin American independence and expanding British maritime reach. He later wrote reflective essays on naval life and travel method.

He stands among the officer-authors who turned wartime and peacetime cruising into a literature of global reconnaissance for the British public.
